basis: close decision -> next open fill, 10bp per side, top-N equal weight
caveats: the static arms ride class equal-weight indices that rebalance daily at ZERO cost (etf_equity_alpha.ew_universe); a real passive holder pays something, so the premium measured here is a LOWER bound on what the ranking adds

the static class shape comes from the fully-invested attribution chain; both arms carry the same 8% overlay, and read.vol_delivered reports what each one actually delivered so the comparison is checkable rather than assumed
both arms draw on the same ETF pool, so the survivorship bias that inflates the equity sleeve inflates the static mix as well -- it cancels in the premium, not in the absolute numbers

one regime: the premium is measured on the 2020+ window the book was published on; r1305 showed the same engine loses to equal weight before 2020, and this script does not re-price the static mix on that window

control.note: the compared arm is the arm that was published

engine: etf_book_production.prep_panel + etf_robust_pf.open_to_open_equity (control) / etf_equity_alpha.ew_universe (static arms); no re-implementation
question: does the shipped book beat holding its own class exposure statically, with no scoring and no rotation?

read.verdict: the ranking pays: +6.36pp/yr over a static mix of the book's own class exposure, at 10.46x the static arm's turnover

static_weight_source: mean class shape of etf_equity_alpha.run_with_attribution (fully-invested chain); both arms carry the same 8% overlay, delivered vol per arm is in read.vol_delivered
vol_overlay: scale = min(1, 0.08 / backward 60d realised vol) at each decision
